summary: Start the day at Wat Phra Singh Woramahawihan, a major active Lanna temple in Chiang Mai’s Old City. Its gilded chedi and Viharn Lai Kham make a focused, walkable visit; arriving near opening offers a quieter atmosphere, but visitors should not expect to observe a scheduled chanting service.
whyGo: See one of Chiang Mai’s most important temples and the revered Phra Phuttha Sihing image in Viharn Lai Kham.
Enjoy the historic architecture and courtyard before the busiest daytime tour hours.
Walk here from Old City accommodation and continue to nearby heritage sights afterward.
bestFor: First-time visitors interested in Lanna architecture and an active Buddhist temple
Travellers who want a short, quiet start to a day in the Old City
People comfortable observing worship respectfully without expecting a guided ceremony
skipIf: You need a guaranteed opportunity to attend or photograph monk chanting; no public timetable was verified.
You prefer a remote or secluded temple experience; this is a prominent city temple.
You require verified step-free access to every hall; detailed access information was not available.
duration: Planning estimate: 45–90 minutes for the main compound and accessible open halls; allow extra time for a quiet sit or nearby Old City walk.
cost: The Tourism Authority of Thailand’s Japan office currently lists ฿50 admission. Confirm the fee and which halls it covers at the entrance; donations and transport are extra.
hours: The Tourism Authority of Thailand’s Japan office lists daily hours of 07:00–22:00. This is the compound listing; individual halls may open or close on different schedules. No public monk-chanting hours were verified.
bestTime: Arrive around opening, about 07:00, for cooler weather and a better chance of a calm courtyard. Treat any worship underway as private religious practice: observe quietly from an appropriate distance and do not approach or photograph participants without permission.
gettingThere: At 2 Sam Lan Road in the Old City. The TAT Japan office says it is about 10–15 minutes by songthaew from central Chiang Mai; if staying inside the Old City, walking is often practical. Agree any songthaew fare before boarding. Traffic and pickup location affect travel time.
booking: No advance booking is listed for an ordinary visit. Check at the gate for temporary closures or access restrictions, especially if you hope to enter a particular hall.
accessibility: No detailed accessibility information was found in the sources reviewed. The large compound includes multiple halls and outdoor paths; surfaces, steps and access to individual buildings may vary. Ask at the entrance about a step-free route and seating if needed.
practicalTips: Wear clothing that covers shoulders and knees; remove shoes before entering halls where indicated.
Silence your phone, speak quietly, and follow signs or staff instructions; the government’s temple guide advises against photographing people engaged in worship without permission.
Do not touch Buddha images or climb on historic structures; ask before photographing monks or worshippers.
Carry small cash for the listed admission and optional donation.
decemberNotes: December is generally a cooler, popular period for Chiang Mai sightseeing, so an opening-time visit can be more comfortable than midday. This is seasonal guidance, not a December 2026 forecast. No December 2026 closure or special service schedule was verified; recheck locally shortly before visiting.
uncertainties: The listed ฿50 fee and 07:00–22:00 hours are from the Tourism Authority of Thailand’s Japan office page; confirm locally because official listings can change and hall access may differ.
The temple’s public monk-chanting schedule, if visitors may attend, could not be verified. Do not plan around seeing chanting without checking directly.
Step-free access and December 2026 special hours or events were not confirmed.
